cycles.method: static: tools/build/cycle_count.py on the author's test remix, the dearest path of the per-sample loop (SHIFT), 416 cycles/sample; RING is about 240 by the author's count. measured: modules/lofi2/perf.py bench, benchmark_reverbs.run as benchmark_stock_dsp.py runs it (one instance per core at positions 0 and 4, audio at X:0, 4,096 blocks of 16 frames, the null stub's peak subtracted) on the private native image cd0f7d5a... (octabam 7795adf0, LOFI2 0.1.1; rerun 21 Oct 2026, every figure recorded here equal to the runs on ddcd3473... (8250be0c, 0.1.0) and 3d63406d... (21f6de90)) Worst of 66 LOFI2 cases: the manifest's dearest settings in SHIFT DOWN with a trig split at frame 1, 430.06 executed instructions/sample (406.44 unsplit; SHIFT UP 429.31 / 406.06; RING 274.31 / 251.06; defaults 249.88). Executed instructions in dsp_host, not chip cycles; no stalls modelled.

stock.baseline: perf.py bench: LO-FI, SPRING REV, DARK REV and DJ EQ run on the original image through the same cases as LOFI2 (fixed, the moving pattern, and a trig split at every position 1-15). Unsplit they reproduce benchmark_stock_dsp.py's figures as E-Verb's record quotes them (SPRING REV 257.5, DARK REV 193.25, DJ EQ 293.38); LO-FI unsplit is 275.44.
stock.justification: LOFI2 does what stock LO-FI does (sample-rate and bit reduction on the same curves, a ring modulator) and adds a stereo frequency shifter: two four-section Hilbert allpass pairs per channel sharing one quadrature oscillator, with feedback, plus a first-order shelf and glides on nine knobs. The shifter is what costs: SHIFT's worst case 430.06 is 1.48x LO-FI (290.06), 1.37x SPRING REV (314.19, the cost target for new FX) and 1.30x DJ EQ (330.94, the dearest stock effect). In RING, which is the part stock LO-FI also has, it is 274.31: 0.95x LO-FI and 0.87x SPRING REV. This is the author's optimisation of the first merged module (654 -> 416 static cycles, 596 -> 430 executed). Four instances per core are 4 x 416 = 1,664 of the 3,120 usable static cycles; the author reports eight instances at once, four per core, in UP, DOWN and RING on his MKII with this source in his octabam build.

stress.method: modules/lofi2/perf.py stress. The load stress_project.py describes, driven straight into dsp_host on the private native image cd0f7d5a... (octabam 7795adf0, LOFI2 0.1.1; rerun 21 Oct 2026, every figure recorded here equal to the runs on ddcd3473... (8250be0c, 0.1.0) and 3d63406d... (21f6de90)): LOFI2 on FX2 of all eight tracks (four per core) behind DJ EQ, the dearest stock effect, on every FX1; per block, three LFOs (sine, triangle, square) on LOFI2's FREQ, SRR and LPF, and a new random value on every slot of both effects each sixteenth at 120 BPM: 14 slots changed per step (LOFI2's nine, MODE and RNGE included so the modes switch under load, and DJ EQ's five), of which 11 can be locked on a unit (LOFI2's three SETUP knobs change only with Parts there); trig splits of 1, 3, 7, 8, 12 and 15 frames on six tracks; eight different 32 s stems plus a 2 s tail; dsp_host -guard 0x4000 -guard-shared -dirty 0x5a. Result: host exit 0, no hang; LOFI2's eight instances 0 stray write regions and 0 clobbers (the stock DJ EQs write their own scratch, 0 clobbers); 16 guarded instances; per-core peak 3013.9 and 3014.1 executed instructions/sample with all sixteen effects. It exercises the DSP side only: the firmware's own LFO and lock delivery, Part switches and the ColdFire side are not in it.
